claims.assertion: The driver was never physically blocked from the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 0 m at 08:43:00 and he was stationary at 0 m from the pickup for the full 8 min 0 s before he cancelled.

The driver did satisfy the arrival and waiting machinery — first within 200 m at 08:41:00, cumulative 10 min 0 s inside 200 m, platform auto-confirmed arrival at 08:43:00 and waited 8 min 0 s after the tap — so the case cannot be won by the driver on a failure of the NS-1 arrival conditions.
The cancellation fee actually on record is $5.00, not the $6.61 cancellation fee the policy provides for, so the sum charged does not match any fee the no-show policy authorises.
The platform's own wait timer ran a 5 min 0 s free period and applied the fee at 08:51:00, i.e. the charge was generated by the app's timer rather than by any rider no-show.

Every message and call in the in-app chat came from the driver (4 messages, 1 call) and none was answered; the rider never told the driver she was present at a specific spot, so nothing in the chat establishes that she was located where the driver searched.

No traffic or weather condition prevented the driver from completing the pickup — no speed band records, no incidents near the route, and no rain — so the driver had no external justification for cancelling after waiting.

The driver cancelled without a claimed valid reason being made out against the rider, which under NS-3 means the rider bears no cancellation fee at all and any amount already deducted is refundable in full.
The driver's record (900 days, 4.9 rating, 3201 trips, 0 upheld disputes) shows no pattern on his side, so this is best resolved as a single contested $5.00 charge rather than an account action.

weaknesses: The driver's GPS placed him at 0 m from the pickup and stationary for 8 min 0 s (F1, F3) while the rider sent no message and did not answer the call (F15); the driver will argue this is textbook NS-1 riding — arrival confirmed, >3 min wait — and that the rider simply failed to show.

The rider's own account says she waited 10 minutes 'at the lobby', but the only lobby reference in the record is the driver's claim that he was at the lobby (F11); there is no GPS or chat evidence of where the rider stood, and the driver's offered plate/description (F11) was never answered by the rider.

The rider's profile looks poor by comparison: rating 3.9 with 4 disputes in 90 days (F19), which the driver will use to argue the complaint is habitual rather than meritorious — though it cannot decide the case on its own.

The exact fee is $5.00 (F8), which fits the NS-6 wait-fee/voucher figure rather than the $6.61 cancellation fee the policy authorises (F4); the rider's characterisation of it as a 'cancellation fee' is therefore inaccurate and the precise clause footing is contested.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded: the GPS does show the driver at 0 m from the pickup (F1) and stationary there for 8 min 0 s (F3) — my case is not that he failed to reach the point, but that his presence there does not by itself transfer liability to a rider who was also there and never rode. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
→ D2 (concedes): Conceded: 10 min 0 s cumulative within 200 m (F2) satisfies NS-1 (ii), so the driver's arrival range is not in dispute; the disputed element is what fee, if any, follows. [F2] [NS-1]
→ D3: The system did recognise arrival (F6) and ran its timer 08:43:10–08:48:10 (F7), but that is the platform's own automated machinery, not an NS-1 'I'm Here' press by the driver, and NS-6 requires the driver to tap the fee button at drop-off on a completed trip — which never happened here (F4). [F6 F7 F4] [NS-1 NS-6]
→ D4: Waiting > 3 minutes shows only that the driver waited; NS-1 also requires that he waited for the rider, and the record shows he cancelled the trip himself 8 min 0 s after arrival without the rider ever boarding (F5, F4). [F3 F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-6]
→ D5: The driver's 4 messages and 1 unanswered call (F10–F15) prove effort, not rider absence on their own, and nothing in them records the rider's location — his own 'lobby area' description (F11) is his claim, uncorroborated by any GPS of the rider. [F10 F11 F12 F13 F14 F15] [NS-1]

→ D7: This is where the driver's case fails on its own numbers: the charge on record is $5.00 (F8), and the $5.00 item is the waiting fee, whose condition — the rider boarding and the trip being completed — is expressly absent here because the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 (F4); the $6.61 fee the driver invokes is not the one charged. [F8 F4] [NS-6 NS-1 FARE-1]
→ D8: Surge is 1.0× and $5.00 is the only disputed sum (F8, F9), which is precisely why it must be refunded rather than left standing — a $5.00 charge that matches no satisfied fee condition is an unpublished/unfounded add-on under FARE-1. [F8 F9] [FARE-1 NS-6]
→ D9: I do not seek any account flag against the driver — his record is clean (F20) — and I equally ask the judge to disregard the rider's history (F19), since profile facts cannot decide this case. [F19 F20] [RD-6]
Revised ask: refund_full $5.00
